messages.author: 97dd7aacdca5ec80
messages.subject: How to obtain tSNE plots
parts:
I am trying to get clustering based on tSNE, where the cell types can be viewed as clusters. However, I only have single cell expression data and no tsne_1 or tsne_2 values saved as pdata (as given in the example). I am getting all other results but not the tsne values. Is it possible to obtain the plots without having the "pdata.txt"'s all column values (as I just have 'cell' information). I am providing a code, where I intentionally not used all values from pdata.txt (this example replicates the only data I have for Arabidopsis). Thanks for taking time to read the post. It would be a great assistance if you could help me.

library(garnett)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(ggplot2)
> mat <- readMM(system.file("extdata", "exprs_sparse.mtx", package = "garnett"))
> fdata <- read.table(system.file("extdata", "fdata.txt", package = "garnett"))
> pdata <- read.table(system.file("extdata", "pdata.txt", package = "garnett"),sep="\t")
> row.names(mat) <- row.names(fdata)
> colnames(mat) <- row.names(pdata)
>
>
>
> h_sheet <- read.delim("/home/rahul/human_pdata_new.txt",row.names=1)
>
> h_annotation <- read.delim("/home/rahul/human_fdata_new.txt",row.names=1)
>
> head(h_sheet)
                            cells
AAGCACTGCACACA-1 AAGCACTGCACACA-1
GGCTCACTGGTCTA-1 GGCTCACTGGTCTA-1
AGCACTGATATCTC-1 AGCACTGATATCTC-1
ACACGTGATATTCC-1 ACACGTGATATTCC-1
ATATGCCTCTGCAA-1 ATATGCCTCTGCAA-1
TGACGAACCTATTC-1 TGACGAACCTATTC-1
> head(h_annotation)
             gene_short_name
MIR1302-10        MIR1302-10
FAM138A              FAM138A
OR4F5                  OR4F5
RP11-34P13.7    RP11-34P13.7
RP11-34P13.8    RP11-34P13.8
AL627309.1        AL627309.1
>
> pd <- new("AnnotatedDataFrame", data =h_sheet )
> fd <- new("AnnotatedDataFrame", data = h_annotation)
>
> pbmc_cds <- newCellDataSet(as.matrix(mat),  phenoData = pd, featureData = fd)
>
>
> pbmc_cds <- estimateSizeFactors(pbmc_cds)
>
> set.seed(260)
>
>
> pbmc_classifier <- train_cell_classifier(cds = pbmc_cds,
+                                          marker_file = '/home/rahul/hsPBMC_markers.txt',
+                                          db=org.Hs.eg.db,
+                                          cds_gene_id_type = "SYMBOL",
+                                          num_unknown = 50,
+                                          marker_file_gene_id_type = "SYMBOL")
There are 8 cell type definitions
training_sample
        B cells Dendritic cells         T cells         Unknown
            263              12             328              50
Model training finished.
training_sample
CD4 T cells CD8 T cells     Unknown
        118          56          50
Model training finished.
>
> pbmc_cds <- classify_cells(pbmc_cds, pbmc_classifier,
+                            db = org.Hs.eg.db,
+                            cluster_extend = TRUE,
+                            cds_gene_id_type = "SYMBOL")
> head(pData(pbmc_cds))
                            cells Size_Factor garnett_cluster       cell_type cluster_ext_type
AAGCACTGCACACA-1 AAGCACTGCACACA-1   0.5591814               1         B cells          B cells
GGCTCACTGGTCTA-1 GGCTCACTGGTCTA-1   0.5159340               1         Unknown          Unknown
AGCACTGATATCTC-1 AGCACTGATATCTC-1   0.6980284               1         B cells          B cells
ACACGTGATATTCC-1 ACACGTGATATTCC-1   0.8156310               1         B cells          B cells

TGACGAACCTATTC-1 TGACGAACCTATTC-1   0.6494699               2 Dendritic cells  Dendritic cells
>
>
> qplot(tsne_1, tsne_2, color = cell_type, data = pData(pbmc_cds)) + theme_bw()
Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : object 'tsne_1' not found
>
> qplot(tsne_1, tsne_2, color = cluster_ext_type, data = pData(pbmc_cds)) + theme_bw()
Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : object 'tsne_1' not found

messages.author: 085d3d5aaca33554
messages.subject: Re: How to obtain tSNE plots
parts:
You can use Monocle to calculate your own tSNE coordinates, see here:
http://cole-trapnell-lab.github.io/monocle-release/docs/#clustering-cells

Monocle stores the tSNE coordinates internally, so you'll need to extract them using:
tsne_coords <- t(reducedDimA(input_cds))
row.names(tsne_coords) <- row.names(pData(input_cds))

messages.author: 027760d088a56515
messages.subject: Re: How to obtain tSNE plots
parts:
Either of the plotting methods you mention will work. You can plot them using plot_cell_clusters in monocle, or you can extract the tSNE coordinates from your cds object and plot them using ggplot. To extract tSNE coordinates from monocle's cds object, this should work:

pData(cds)$tsne_1 <- reducedDimA(cds)[1,]
pData(cds)$tsne_2 <- reducedDimA(cds)[2,]
